output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: `currentDir` (parent directory of a resource, taken directly from an HTTP request parameter) was concatenated into `fullName` at ResourcesServiceImpl.java lines ~140, ~217, and ~973 without any traversal check, while only the sibling leaf `name`/`fileName` was checked via `FileUtils.directoryTraversal(name)`. `fullName` is then persisted and passed unchanged into HadoopUtils path-construction methods (`getHdfsFileName`/`getHdfsResourceFileName` -> `new Path(...)` inside `mkdir`/`copy`/`copyLocalToHdfs`/`delete`), letting a payload like `currentDir=/pov/../../../../../../../../tmp/dolphin_pwn` escape the tenant's HDFS resource root.

Fix: added `FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String dirPath)` — a sibling of the existing single-segment `directoryTraversal(String)` — that splits a "/"-separated directory path and rejects it if any segment is literally ".." (after trimming) or if it contains a backslash (defense against alternate-separator smuggling). Wired this check into the three service methods that accept a raw `currentDir` before it is ever used to build `fullName`: `createDirectory`, `createResource`, and `onlineCreateResource`. Because `updateResource` and all the internal rename/copy/delete/upload helpers reuse the already-validated `fullName` (they never re-derive a path from a fresh, unvalidated `currentDir`), gating these three entry points closes every sink path enumerated in the alert (the delete-on-conflict branch in `createDirectory`, the HDFS copy in `createResource`/`updateResource`, `uploadContentToHdfs` in `onlineCreateResource`, and the rename/move helpers) with a single root-cause fix at the trust boundary, matching the existing pattern used for `name` validation.

Tests added:
- `FileUtilsTest.testDirectoryPathTraversal` (dolphinscheduler-common) — exercises the real (unmocked) algorithm against legitimate paths, various ".." placements (including the exact POV payload), and backslash/null inputs.
- `ResourcesServiceTest.testCreateDirectoryCurrentDirPathTraversal`, `testCreateResourceCurrentDirPathTraversal`, `testOnlineCreateResourceCurrentDirPathTraversal` (dolphinscheduler-api) — wiring-level tests confirming each entry point returns `Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` and never reaches `resourcesMapper.insert(...)` when the new check fires.

Note on regression commands: this repo's Docker image lacks the JUnit-vintage engine, so plain `mvn test` silently discovers 0 of the JUnit4+PowerMock tests here (a pre-existing environment limitation, also documented in `.security-pipeline/pov/run_pov.sh`). The regression commands above therefore compile the module and invoke `org.junit.runner.JUnitCore` directly against the specific test classes, exactly like the POV harness does — this was verified to actually execute and pass all tests (19/19 in ResourcesServiceTest, 8/8 in FileUtilsTest) both before finalizing.
regression_commands: EXT="$(tr ':' '\n' < .security-pipeline/pov/cp.txt | grep -v '/org/apache/dolphinscheduler/' | paste -sd: -)"; DS="$(find . -type d -path '*/target/classes' | paste -sd: -)"; CP="dolphinscheduler-api/target/test-classes:dolphinscheduler-api/target/classes:dolphinscheduler-common/target/test-classes:${DS}:${EXT}"; java -cp "$CP" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore org.apache.dolphinscheduler.api.service.ResourcesServiceTest

EXT="$(tr ':' '\n' < .security-pipeline/pov/cp.txt | grep -v '/org/apache/dolphinscheduler/' | paste -sd: -)"; DS="$(find . -type d -path '*/target/classes' | paste -sd: -)"; CP="dolphinscheduler-api/target/test-classes:dolphinscheduler-api/target/classes:dolphinscheduler-common/target/test-classes:${DS}:${EXT}"; java -cp "$CP" org.junit.runner.JUnitCore org.apache.dolphinscheduler.common.utils.FileUtilsTest
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change is narrowly scoped: `currentDir` values containing a literal ".." path segment (or a backslash) are now rejected with the same `VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` status already used for invalid `name` values, on createDirectory/createResource/onlineCreateResource only. Legitimate currentDir values ("/", "/a", "/a/b/c", including names that merely contain ".." as a substring like "a..b" which is NOT an exact ".." segment) are unaffected — verified by both the new unit test and the fact all pre-existing ResourcesServiceTest cases (which all use "/" as currentDir) still pass unchanged. updateResource/rename/copy/delete paths were intentionally left untouched since they operate on `fullName` values that were already validated at creation time; no new check was needed there. Full `mvn -DskipTests package` reactor build succeeds; the previously-passing POV now fails (exploit blocked) with `Status.VERIFY_PARAMETER_NAME_FAILED` returned before any DB write or HDFS call.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-022 path traversal in DolphinScheduler's resource center: ResourcesServiceImpl validated only the leaf `name`/`fileName` parameter via FileUtils.directoryTraversal(), but never validated the attacker-controlled parent-directory `currentDir` parameter before concatenating it into `fullName` and handing that to HadoopUtils path-construction sinks (mkdir/copy/copyLocalToHdfs). Added a new FileUtils.directoryPathTraversal(String) helper that rejects any ".." path segment (and backslashes) in a multi-segment directory path, and call it at the trust boundary in all three public entry points that accept a raw `currentDir`: createDirectory, createResource, and onlineCreateResource. This blocks the POV's traversal payload and, because updateResource/rename/copy/upload internally reuse the already-validated `fullName` derived from these three entry points (never re-deriving from a fresh unvalidated currentDir), it also closes the other sink paths listed in the alert (createDirectory's delete-on-conflict path, createResource/updateResource's HDFS copy, onlineCreateResource's uploadContentToHdfs, and the rename/move helpers) without needing separate checks at each of them.
